subject: Dedicated reservation: smoothing schedule options and minimum GPU floor for PolarisAI
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@polaris.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation: smoothing schedule options and minimum GPU floor for PolarisAI

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on PolarisAI's QPS and model mix (1x LLM-heavy gen model + 2 smaller embed/rerank models) I sketched three commitment smoothing options that balance predictable unit economics with the ability to burst for weekly peak training jobs. Attached is a spreadsheet with line-item pricing and a sample Mutual Action Plan (MAP). Highlights below: please review and tell us which tradeoffs feel right.

Option A — Conservative floor (Best for predictable ops)
- Minimum committed: 40 GPUs (H100-equivalent)
- Ramp: 10 GPUs active month 1, +10 month 3, +10 month 5, reach floor by month 7
- Burst pool: +20 GPUs (on-demand, billed at burst rate; 72hr pre-warm)
- Ideal if you want consistent latency SLOs for prod traffic and prefer lower on-demand spend variance

Option B — Smoothing with seasonal buffer (Balanced)
- Minimum committed: 25 GPUs
- Ramp: 15 GPUs month 1, add 5 GPUs month 4, 5 GPUs month 8
- Burst pool: +30 GPUs with hourly autoscale and sustained-burst discounts after 48h
- Good if you expect a strong ramp in NRT usage but want to keep upfront spend moderate

Option C — Aggressive on-demand-first (Low commitment)
- Minimum committed: 10 GPUs
- Ramp: flexible; target to convert to 30 GPUs once 90-day utilization > 65%
- Burst pool: +40 GPUs; recommended for proof-of-concept/smaller initial footprint

Operational notes: all options include:
- Region: primary us-west, with cross-region failover to us-east for SLA-critical routes
- Kernel/instance mix: we recommend H100s for the gen cascade, A10G for embedding lanes if cost efficiency is primary
- KV cache warmup policy: 24–48h pre-warm for model-specific prefixes to hit 60–70% cache hit rate during steady-state
- Autoscaling triggers and throttles are in the MAP draft (attached)

Next steps: which option aligns with PolarisAI procurement appetite? If B or C, we can draft a 60-day conversion credit that applies to the committed pool when you convert from on-demand.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive — Dedicated & Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Naomi —

Appreciate the quick summary. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we share with procurement:
1) The H100 vs A100 note — can you provide the unit-perf delta you used to convert to H100-equivalent GPUs in the spreadsheet? We want to sanity-check throughput assumptions.
2) For Option B, how does the sustained-burst discount apply if we exceed burst for more than 72 hours? Is there an automatic conversion to committed at a pro-rated rate or do we need an explicit amendment?
3) Can you confirm whether the KMS/HSM integration is available in the us-west region for dedicated pools? Our security team insists on customer-controlled keys.

Also — our ML platform team asked for an example utilization heatmap (sample 7-day) to validate the ramp cadence. Can you attach a representative heatmap?

Thanks,

PolarisAI

Hi Liam —

Answers inline:
1) H100-equivalent conversions: we normalize to an H100 baseline for gen workloads. In the spreadsheet, 1 H100-equivalent = 
   - ~1.9x A100-80GB for attention-heavy long-seq gen
   - ~2.6x for int8 quantized smaller models where kernel efficiency differs
   The sheet includes per-model perf multipliers we used — see tab "Perf_Assumptions". If you want, Marcus can run a short perf test against your model artifact to lock the numbers.

2) Sustained-burst handling: for Option B we automatically apply a sustained-burst discount tier after 48 continuous hours at 50% of committed pool (the discount schedule is in the pricing tab). If usage remains above the sustained threshold for 14 continuous days we provide an automatic conversion credit that can be applied when you sign an amendment to increase committed GPUs (requires mutual acceptance in the MAP). We avoid forced conversions to respect procurement cadence.

3) KMS/HSM: yes — customer KMS integration is supported in us-west dedicated clusters. For HSM-backed keys we have a short onboarding checklist (I attached the MAP with the security appendix).

I attached a sample 7-day utilization heatmap (utilization-sample-heatmap.png) that mirrors a customer with similar gen+embed mix. It shows pronounced nightly training jobs (peaks) and a stable daytime inference baseline.

If you want a perf-validation run, I can have Marcus schedule a 2-hour validation slot next week; he'll need an access token and a small model artifact or a docker image of your model.

Thanks — any preferred time for the validation?

Naomi

Hey Liam —

I'll run the perf validation once you confirm the model artifact. A couple of commercial notes from pricing:
- We can offer a 10% credit on transient burst hours for the first 90 days if you commit to Option B (25 GPUs). The credit applies during periods when average pool utilization across committed+burst exceeds 70%.
- For bookkeeping: our standard MAP milestone for activation is signed SOW + initial 30% of the first month committed value; we can defer the first month for PoC customers but not for committed contracts.
- SLA: committed pools include a 10ms p50 improvement baseline for cached inference paths and a 99.9% availability SLA. Cross-region failover is included as an add-on if you want a guaranteed RPO/RTO in the MAP.

If procurement needs a single-sheet summary, I attached a draft MAP to the Drive link Naomi shared. Once you pick an option we'll prepare an SOW that maps committed GPU months to amortized list price and shows the conversion credit schedule.
